relationships.rationale: This indicative-content block addresses how an animal responds to vaccination.
The secondary immune response is part of the requested explanation of animals' response following vaccination.
This block directly addresses prevention of food poisoning in humans.
The rule limits Level 2 to responses that link animal immunity to prevention of a human outbreak.
The statement that responses are marked holistically applies to assigning Level 1.
The statement that responses are marked holistically applies to assigning Level 2.
It explains that 'indicative content' means the listed points are not exhaustive and other suitable ideas may receive credit.
It specifies that the Level 2 link must cover primary and secondary animal responses as well as prevention of human infection.
It adds that Level 2 requires newly produced antibodies rather than antibodies merely remaining from the primary response.
It makes clear that antibodies produced during the secondary response are newly made antibodies.
It specifies that Level 1 credit requires descriptions of both primary and secondary animal responses.
Its terminology guidance concerns the point crediting white blood cells or lymphocytes.
Its terminology guidance also concerns the point referring to white blood cells killing Salmonella.
It explains that using the full term anywhere in the response is sufficient when the abbreviation WBC is also used.
It provides the conditional exception that WBC is acceptable from its second occurrence even if the full term is absent.
It identifies lymphocytes as an acceptable alternative to the term white blood cells.
It excludes an answer consistently substituting virus for bacteria from Level 2 by capping it at Level 1.
